added_failures_note: The reviewed run's manifest carries no baseline_suite or after_suite arms, and this review round covers only a51678ba2..da576d4bd, so there is no base/head suite pair to take a set difference over and no added failure id can be derived. The landed change touches one benchmark module and three evidence files; nothing in tests/ imports it. The zero is a measured absence of a suite arm, not a green delta.

findings.text: The tests line is a template rather than the literal command: it carries <worktree>, <probe> and <scratch> unsubstituted plus trailing prose ('run twice: once from revision ...'), and the committed gate log carries no '# command:' header to fall back on, so promotion cannot fill a re-runnable receipt from it and refuses the line on shape.

persist() writes its scratch file and replaces the target itself, duplicating the atomic JSON writer the repository already owns at nova/io/json.py:12 (write_atomic) and the sibling copy at benchmarks/compile_host_memory.py:56; the new copy extends neither and drops write_atomic's fsync of both the file and its directory, so the durability module a reader is told this follows is actually less durable than the owner it duplicates.

The banner records revision a51678ba2, but the code that produced this log is the repaired file (the log's LEDGER lines are printed only by persist(), which a51678ba2 at benchmarks/forward_solve_memory_ledger.py:424 does not have; its single write is the last statement of main()), so the evidence artifact names a revision that cannot produce it, and a reader checking out the named sha cannot reproduce the log.

The control's failing arm - the same command run from the pre-repair revision leaving its output directory empty - is asserted in prose only; no log, listing or exit record for that arm is committed, so the negative control rests on the worker's account for the half that has to fail rather than on an artifact a reader can inspect.

negative_control_log names two files joined by 'and' ('...interrupted-run.log and interrupted-run-ledger.json), not the single bare path the field contract requires, so a reader or check that opens the line as a path resolves nothing.

item_verdicts.call_sites: Searched nova/, tests/, scripts/, benchmarks/, docs/ and apps/ for references to forward_solve_memory_ledger; nothing imports the module and nothing references it outside its own file, so it has no production call site.
item_verdicts.diff: Read both commits against a51678ba2: a76a85190 adds persist() and census() plus a SIGTERM handler and calls them from begin(), end() and the three census sites, and removes the single end-of-main write; da576d4bd adds one paragraph to docs/research/forward-solve-memory-ledger.html:125 and the README and the two interrupted-run evidence files, with several unrelated ruff-format-only line reflows in the source file.
item_verdicts.done_when: The done_when for this round is that a run stopped before the end of main() still writes the ledger; the gate is the controlled interrupted run recorded in docs/research/forward-solve-memory-ledger/README.md:7-12 and manifest.md:20, and the committed ledger (interrupted-run-ledger.json) carries completed:false, stop_signal:SIGTERM, nine phases_completed and census_inflight:after-warm-execute, which is the measure the finding named; the failing arm of the control is asserted in prose only, with no committed log or listing for it.
item_verdicts.goal: The source goal (brief.md done-when 1) asks that the probe write its ledger under docs/research/forward-solve-memory-ledger/ and attribute the memory; the two commits gained since the prior review (a76a85190, da576d4bd) make benchmarks/forward_solve_memory_ledger.py persist that ledger at every phase boundary and on SIGTERM, and land the interrupted-run ledger and README under docs/research/forward-solve-memory-ledger/, so the persistence half of the goal is met and the round answers the prior review's one blocking finding.
item_verdicts.manifest: Read manifest.md; it records status complete, commits 942b8b99f..da576d4bd, the repair note for finding f03dff54d67, and the negative-control note, but its tests line at manifest.md:20 is a template carrying <worktree>, <probe> and <scratch> placeholders with trailing prose, and its negative_control_log at manifest.md:22 names two path-like phrases joined by 'and' rather than one bare path.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The declared write paths are benchmarks/forward_solve_memory_ledger.py, docs/research/forward-solve-memory-ledger.html and docs/research/forward-solve-memory-ledger; git diff --stat a51678ba2..da576d4bd reports exactly five paths, all inside that fence (forward_solve_memory_ledger.py, the .html, and README.md plus the two interrupted-run evidence files under the directory), with no product source touched.

notes.negative_control_reproduction: The pre-existing defect was re-read rather than re-run: git show a51678ba2:benchmarks/forward_solve_memory_ledger.py:424 is the only ledger write and it is the last statement of main(), so a SIGTERM during any earlier phase writes nothing - the reproduction the committed interrupted run demonstrates at the repaired head.
notes.no_negative_control_run: No mutation was applied by this review; this is a reading review and the reading bound held.
notes.reuse_search: Searched benchmarks/ and nova/ for an atomic JSON receipt writer; nova/io/json.py:12 write_atomic is the owning mechanism, and benchmarks/compile_host_memory.py:56 _write_json is the older in-repo copy the reviewed docstring names. The new persist() extends neither.
notes.review_scope: Read the source brief and manifest, the prior review record at review-records/r-20261103T062144710604-forward-solve-memory-ledger.at-a51678ba2a013ad537d88f81b41d3071f1c75a7f.json, both commits a51678ba2..da576d4bd, the committed interrupted-run.log and interrupted-run-ledger.json, and the one owner read the reuse bound allows: nova/io/json.py:12-46 (write_atomic) alongside benchmarks/compile_host_memory.py:56-62, which the reviewed diff cites as its pattern.
